note: real pgp mainnet headers, extracted from a synced datadir; extraData is the serialized ELA payload.Confirm. vectorsDigest = sha256 over the canonical JSON of the vectors array (compact separators, keys sorted) = 81619f5aeaeb64513624354353c5c42059cdbf1dc23c52d1523100337b66d033 (82641 bytes); editing the notes must not change it. Reproducible from Python with json.dumps(vectors, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) and from Go with json.Unmarshal into any followed by json.Marshal (map keys get sorted, Marshal is already compact; both verified byte-exact). NOT reproducible from a typed struct: Go emits struct declaration order, omitempty drops zero values, and Marshal HTML-escapes <, > and & (the vectors currently contain none of the three, which the matching Go digest already implies). The digest covers the vectors array only, never the note fields, so the notes can be reworded freely - but any actual data must live in the vectors, where this digest protects it
signatureSchemeNote: ELA crypto.Verify: NIST P-256 (elliptic.P256), digest = SHA-256(SerializeUnsigned), signature = r||s 32+32 bytes, public key = 33-byte compressed P-256 point. vote.proposalHash = SHA-256d(proposal.SerializeUnsigned) and equals proposal.Hash().
confirmEncodingNote: header.Extra mixes two length encodings in one struct: the vote count is a fixed 8-byte little-endian uint64 (common.WriteUint64, Elastos.ELA/common/serialize.go), while the VarBytes fields (sponsor, sign, signer) carry a variable-length Bitcoin CompactSize prefix. Reading the vote count as a varint consumes 1 byte instead of 8, so the 7 remaining 0x00 bytes of that uint64 are parsed as the start of the next field and everything after is shifted 7 bytes: every length prefix and every signature then looks corrupt while the bytes on the wire are valid. Only the VarBytes fields are varint-prefixed
majorityNote: mainnet has 12 producers, minSignCount = int(12*2/3) = 8, and every legacy block carries exactly 8 votes from 8 distinct signers. The check is validVotes < minSignCount, so exactly 8 passes; an implementation using > (9 votes) or ceil(2/3) rejects 100% of mainnet blocks. The sponsor is necessarily one of the 8 voters: the proposer starts the proposal and its own vote from the same account (dpos/proposal.go:18, dpos/proposalvote.go:22), so any 'exclude the proposer from the tally' rule would reject all of them too
